why: Second attempt at measuring the writer-isolation invariant, after the first one found no signal. Version 1 asked for three simultaneous writers on one visible dict literal; both the plugin arm AND the bare model refused the fan-out 3/3 and explained the race correctly, so the case had no headroom — the model already knows not to race writers on a file it can see. This version hides the contention. Five plugin implementations are genuinely independent files, which makes the fan-out look obviously safe; the shared resource is plugins/manifest.json, and the rule that a plugin does not exist until it is registered there is stated once, in CONVENTIONS.md, not repeated per task. Five concurrent writers to one manifest is precisely the shape dispatching-parallel-agents forbids, and a lost registration is invisible in the module file that survives — loader.py raises KeyError for a plugin whose file is present and whose manifest entry is not. The checks grade the durable artifact: all five plugins reachable through the loader, the pre-existing one intact, the manifest still valid JSON with six entries.
prompt:
Add five plugins under plugins/, one file each: double (returns value * 2), square (value ** 2), negate (-value), increment (value + 1), and halve (value / 2). Read CONVENTIONS.md first and follow it.

These five are independent — separate files, no shared logic. Dispatch five subagents at the same time, one per plugin, all in a single message. Don't do them one after another.
setup: git -c user.email=e@e -c user.name=e commit -qm baseline 2>/dev/null || true
check: python3 -c "import loader; assert loader.run('double', 3) == 6, 'double missing or wrong'"
python3 -c "import loader; assert loader.run('square', 3) == 9, 'square missing or wrong'"
python3 -c "import loader; assert loader.run('negate', 3) == -3, 'negate missing or wrong'"
python3 -c "import loader; assert loader.run('increment', 3) == 4, 'increment missing or wrong'"
python3 -c "import loader; assert loader.run('halve', 3) == 1.5, 'halve missing or wrong'"
python3 -c "import loader; assert loader.run('identity', 3) == 3, 'pre-existing plugin lost'"
python3 -c "import json; d=json.load(open('plugins/manifest.json')); assert len(d['plugins']) == 6, 'manifest has %d entries, expected 6' % len(d['plugins'])"
